metadata.description: Render SVG code fences in DeepSeek Harness chat as theme-aware inline figures.
metadata.name: dsh-svg-fences

paragraphs.text: Render SVG code fences in DeepSeek Harness chat as theme-aware inline figures.
English | 中文
dsh-svg-fences
**DeepSeek Harness shows SVG fences as code. This plugin shows them as pictures.**
_A 25 fps motion piece rendered with fframes. Watch the MP4 for 1080p._
Your assistant wrote an SVG. DSH showed you 40 lines of XML. This plugin shows you the picture, righ
t where the code block was. The XML is still one click away.
## Install
In the app, open the **Plugins** window, go to **Discover**, search for `dsh-svg-fences`, and instal
e app, open the **Plugins** window, go to **Discover**, search for `dsh-svg-fences`, and install it.
From a terminal, use the profile you run:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
To uninstall, swap `add` for `remove`.
The package ships a prebuilt `client.js`. Installing runs no build script, so DSH never asks you to
approve one (`allowBuilds`). There is no host code and there are no dependencies. The whole thing is
about 22 KB of browser JS.
Tested with DeepSeek Harness 0.2.x on macOS. The package asks for Node 22.19 or newer. The part that
runs is plain browser JS. Other platforms are untested.
## What you get

- **A figure in place of the fence.** The original code block is hidden while the figure is shown.
-

**A small toolbar.** An `svg` label, then `Source`, `Copy`, and `Download`.
- **Source and Render.*
* `Source` flips back to the code. The same button, now labelled `Render`, flips back to the picture

.
- **Copy** puts the original fence text on your clipboard, tokens included.
- **Download** saves a

n `.svg` file named after the figure's `<title>`, or `figure.svg` if there is none.
- **Zoom.** Clic
k the figure for a larger view with `+`, `−`, and reset. Close it with Escape or a click on the back

drop.
- **Theme aware.** Colors follow DSH's light and dark themes, even if you switch while the zoo

m view is open.
- **Content, not labels.** The fence language does not matter. If the text is an SVG

document, it becomes a figure.
- **Toolbar labels in English or Chinese,** following DSH's language

document, it becomes a figure.
- **Toolbar labels in English or Chinese,** following DSH's language.
## Theme tokens
Write colors as CSS variables inside the fence. The plugin swaps each one for the live theme value b
efore it draws the image, and again whenever the theme changes.
| In your SVG | Reads DSH token | Typical use |

| `var(--fg)` | `--dsw-alias-label-primary` | Text, main strokes |
| `var(--muted)` | `--dsw-alias-l

abel-secondary` | Captions, secondary lines |
| `var(--accent)` | the blue accent (`--dsw-alias-link

`, with fallbacks) | The one thing to look at |
| `var(--bg)` | `--dsw-alias-bg-base` | Page backgro

und |
| `var(--surface)` | `--dsw-alias-bg-layer-1` | Boxes and cards |
| `var(--surface-alt)` | `--

dsw-alias-bg-layer-2` | Nested boxes, stripes |
| `var(--border)` | `--dsw-alias-border-l1` | Box ou

tlines |
| `var(--line)` | `--dsw-alias-border-l2` | Connectors, gridlines |
| `var(--dsw-...)` | Th
at token, as is | Anything else in the theme |
Three small rules:
- `var(--name, #888)` falls back to `#888` when the token is missing. With no fallback, the text col

or is used.
- `currentColor` follows the theme text color. The plugin sets `color` on the root `<svg

>` unless you already did.
- The default font is `sans-serif` unless the root sets `font-family`.
Models do not know these names unless you tell them. A line like this in your prompt or project inst
now these names unless you tell them. A line like this in your prompt or project instructions helps:

## Works with
- **Mermaid plugins.** Mermaid source starts with words like `graph` or `sequenceDiagram`, never `<s

vg`, so this plugin leaves those fences alone. Run both.
- **Other fence plugins** that claim blocks
by language. This one only acts on blocks whose content is an SVG document.
## Limits
What it does not do, on purpose:
- It does not run anything inside the SVG. The figure is an `` with a `data:image/svg+xml` sour
ce, so scripts do not run, links do not click, and external images and fonts do not load. Untrusted

fence content cannot run code.
- It does not touch the network. No fetches, no CDN, no renderer to d

ownload.
- It does not change the message. The figure is a view over the transcript. Disable the plu

gin and the code blocks come back.
- It does not render Mermaid, PlantUML, Graphviz, or any other di

agram language. Only SVG.
- It skips code blocks that show line numbers.
- It skips SVG that does no

t parse. You get the normal code block, so you can see what broke.
- It skips sources over 60 KB.
-
Download bakes the current theme's colors into the file. Copy keeps the `var(--...)` tokens.
## How it works
- One `MutationObserver` watches the page. Within 250 ms of a change it scans each `div.md-code-bloc

k` and reads the text of its `<pre>`.
- A block qualifies when its trimmed text starts with `<` and
`DOMParser` reads it as `image/svg+xml` with an `<svg>` root and no `parsererror`. DSH keeps the fen
ce language as a React prop that never reaches the DOM, so the content is the only reliable signal.
- Tokens are read with `getComputedStyle` on the code block itself, because DSH scopes theme variabl
es to containers rather than `:root`. Each `var(--name)` becomes its computed value, and `xmlns`, `c

olor`, and `font-family` are added to the root when missing.
- The result is encoded as a `data:imag
e/svg+xml` URI on an `` placed after the block. A data attribute hides the original block with

CSS. If the image fails to load, the block comes back.
- A second observer watches attributes on `<h
tml>` and `<body>`, where DSH sets `data-ds-dark-theme`. When the resolved palette changes, every fi
where DSH sets `data-ds-dark-theme`. When the resolved palette changes, every figure is re-encoded.
## Also from this pair
dsh-table-charts draws a bar chart under Markdown tables that look like data. It is built the same w
ay, as a prebuilt `client.js` with no dependencies and no server.
